options.name: server
options.label: IPv4 tunnel network
options.note: server mode: network, netmask and optional nopool

options.name: server-ipv6
options.label: IPv6 tunnel network
options.note: IPv6 network for the tunnel

options.name: duplicate-cn
options.label: Allow one identity to connect twice
options.note: allow several sessions with the same identity

options.name: block-ipv6
options.label: Block IPv6 in the tunnel
options.note: drop IPv6 packets at the tunnel, in both directions; no ICMPv6 reply is sent

options.name: route-noexec
options.label: Do not add routes
options.note: do not add routes; only report them on the bus

options.name: ifconfig-noexec
options.label: Do not set up the tun device
options.note: do not configure the interface; only report the settings on the bus

options.name: ifconfig-pool
options.label: IPv4 address range
options.note: set the dynamic address range (overrides the range derived from server)

options.name: route
options.label: IPv4 routes to add
options.note: add a route: network, netmask, gateway, metric

options.name: ifconfig-ipv6-pool
options.label: IPv6 address range
options.note: set the dynamic IPv6 address range

options.name: route-ipv6
options.label: IPv6 routes to add
options.note: add an IPv6 route: prefix, gateway, metric

options.name: client-to-client
options.label: Let clients reach each other
options.note: forward traffic between clients

options.name: mssfix
options.label: Limit the TCP segment size
options.note: clamp the TCP MSS of connections in the tunnel; N is the largest data channel packet, mtu: the largest outer IP packet, fixed: the largest inner packet

options.name: max-clients
options.label: Most clients at one time
options.note: maximum number of concurrent clients (default 1024)

options.name: max-routes-per-client
options.label: Most routes for one client
options.note: maximum number of internal routes per client (default 256)

options.name: ifconfig-pool-persist
options.label: Remember client addresses in a file
options.note: remember client addresses in a file

options.name: route-table
options.label: Routing table
options.note: routing table id for routes (Linux)

options.name: push
options.label: Settings sent to clients
options.note: send an option to clients

options.name: topology
options.label: Topology
options.note: only subnet is accepted; net30 and p2p are not supported

options.name: tun-mtu
options.label: Tunnel MTU
options.note: tunnel MTU, and an optional MTU to announce

options.name: txqueuelen
options.label: Tunnel queue length
options.note: tun transmit queue length

options.name: port
options.label: Port
options.note: local and remote port

options.name: proto
options.label: Protocol
options.note: udp, tcp-client, tcp-server, tls-client or tls-server (TCP in an outer TLS stream, noirvpn to noirvpn), with 4 or 6 for one IP version

options.name: float
options.label: Accept clients from a new address
options.note: accept authenticated packets from a new peer address (server); a client shows a warning that it is not applied

options.name: tls-transport-accept-tcp
options.label: Also accept plain OpenVPN TCP clients
options.note: every proto tls-server listener also accepts raw OpenVPN tcp-client connections on the same port (identified by the first 3 bytes)

options.name: tls-transport-cert
options.label: Certificate of the outer TLS
options.note: certificate (leaf first, then the chain; PEM) for the outer TLS of proto tls-server; default: cert

options.name: inactive
options.label: Disconnect idle clients
options.note: disconnect after n seconds without tunnel traffic; a client only applies it from its own config, and a server ignores it with a warning

options.name: keepalive
options.label: Keepalive (ping, timeout)
options.note: ping interval and timeout; a server pushes them to clients

options.name: tls-transport-key
options.label: Key of the outer TLS
options.note: private key (PEM) for the outer TLS of proto tls-server; default: key

options.name: max-packet-size
options.label: Largest control packet
options.note: control packet size limit; also sets mssfix

options.name: connect-freq-initial
options.label: Limit first replies
options.note: at most n initial replies per sec seconds (UDP)

options.name: connect-freq-source
options.label: Limit first replies for one address
options.note: at most n initial replies for one source address in the connect-freq-initial window (default 20; 0: no limit)

options.name: connect-freq
options.label: Limit new connections
options.note: at most n new connections per sec seconds

options.name: local
options.label: Listen addresses
options.note: local address, port and protocol (a server may list several)

options.name: ping
options.label: Ping interval
options.note: send a ping after n idle seconds

options.name: ping-timer-rem
options.label: Ping only when a peer is known
options.note: run the ping timers only when a peer is known

options.name: rcvbuf
options.label: Receive buffer size
options.note: socket receive buffer size

options.name: ping-restart
options.label: Restart after silence
options.note: restart after n seconds without receiving a packet

options.name: tls-transport-dev
options.label: Second tun device
options.note: name of the second tun device for the proto tls-server clients under datapath dco or udco; default: the dev name with -tls added

options.name: sndbuf
options.label: Send buffer size
options.note: socket send buffer size

options.name: session-timeout
options.label: Session time limit
options.note: end the session after n seconds; a server only applies it in a client-config-dir file, and a client only from its own config

options.name: explicit-exit-notify
options.label: Tell clients when the server stops
options.note: tell the peer when this side stops (UDP)

options.name: tls-transport-ws
options.label: WebSocket path
options.note: send the tls transport in a WebSocket at this path: a tls-client sends the HTTP upgrade request, tls-server and tcp-server listeners respond to it (for a reverse proxy that terminates the outer TLS at the HTTP layer)

options.name: peer-fingerprint
options.label: Accepted certificate fingerprints
options.note: SHA-256 fingerprints of accepted peer certificates

options.name: ca
options.label: CA certificate
options.note: CA certificates (PEM)

options.name: verify-client-cert
options.label: Client certificate check
options.note: require (default), or optional: a client without a certificate logs in with a user name and password (needs peer-passwords or auth-external), and any certificate that is sent must still pass. With no ca, peer-keys or peer-fingerprint, the server does not ask for a certificate at all and only accepts password logins. none is not supported

options.name: auth-external
options.label: Decide logins on the control bus
options.note: ask a bus controller to decide each session; optional timeout in seconds

options.name: extra-certs
options.label: Extra chain certificates
options.note: extra chain certificates to send

options.name: peer-keys-mode
options.label: How a CA and pins work together
options.default: pin, or either with a CA
choices: Default (pin, or either with a CA)
options.note: pin (default), both (chain and pin) or either (a pin, or else a chain); both and either need ca and peer-keys; ca with peer-keys and no mode is the same as either

options.name: askpass
options.label: Key passphrase file
options.note: the passphrase of an encrypted key (key, tls-transport-key): the first line of the file, or typed at the terminal at start-up when no file is given

options.name: peer-passwords
options.label: Password file
options.note: file of user names and password hashes; the server checks the password of a client against it; a password source for verify-client-cert optional

options.name: peer-keys
options.label: Peers file
options.note: peers file: one pinned key per line (username, pin, options)

options.name: remote-cert-tls
options.label: Required certificate type
options.note: the certificate of the peer must have a key usage and the extended key usage of a server (TLS Web Server Authentication) or of a client (TLS Web Client Authentication)

options.name: remote-cert-eku
options.label: Required extended key usage
options.note: the certificate of the peer must have this extended key usage (an OID, or a short or long name)

options.name: remote-cert-ku
options.label: Required key usage
options.note: the certificate of the peer must have a key usage with at least all the bits of one value (hex, 1 to ff, e.g. a0); with no value, it only needs to have a key usage

options.name: verify-x509-name
options.label: Required name in the client certificate
options.note: the certificate of the peer must have this name: the whole subject (type subject, the default), the common name (name) or the start of it (name-prefix); x509-username-field is not applied, so the common name is used

options.name: crl-verify
options.label: Revocation list
options.note: revocation list: a file with CRLs in PEM (reloaded when it changes), or a directory (with the flag dir) with one file per revoked certificate, named by its serial number; checks the peer certificate chain (ca), not peer-fingerprint

options.name: cert
options.label: Server certificate
options.note: our certificate (PEM)

options.name: key
options.label: Server key
options.note: our private key (PEM)

options.name: auth-web
options.label: Web sign-in
options.note: a client that sends IV_SSO=webauth with no certificate and no password waits while the controller handles a web sign-in (needs auth-external and verify-client-cert optional)

options.name: auth
options.label: Control channel digest
options.note: digest for tls-auth; the data channel only uses AEAD

options.name: tls-crypt
options.label: Control channel key (encrypt)
options.note: encrypt and authenticate control packets with a shared key

options.name: tls-auth
options.label: Control channel key (sign)
options.note: HMAC-protect control packets; optional key direction

options.name: tls-crypt-v2
options.label: Control channel keys for each client
options.note: per-client control keys; force-cookie or allow-noncookie on servers

options.name: tls-timeout
options.label: Control packet resend time
options.note: control packet retransmit timeout in seconds

options.name: data-ciphers
options.label: Data channel ciphers
options.note: colon-separated AEAD ciphers in order of preference

options.name: hand-window
options.label: Handshake time limit
options.note: how many seconds a handshake may take

options.name: tls-version-max
options.label: Highest TLS version
options.note: the highest TLS version of the control channel, 1.2 or 1.3

options.name: key-direction
options.label: Key direction
options.note: 0 or 1; selects which halves of the tls-auth key are used

options.name: tls-groups
options.label: Key exchange groups
options.note: allowed TLS key exchange groups

options.name: tls-version-min
options.label: Lowest TLS version
options.note: the lowest TLS version of the control channel, 1.2 or 1.3; 1.0 and 1.1 cause a warning and are treated as 1.2; an unknown version with or-highest is treated as 1.3

options.name: tran-window
options.label: Old key valid time
options.note: seconds an old key stays valid after a renegotiation

options.name: tls-crypt-v2-max-age
options.label: Oldest client key (days)
options.note: reject client keys older than n days

options.name: pq-mode
options.label: Post-quantum key exchange
options.note: off, prefer (default) or require the hybrid post-quantum key exchange

options.name: reneg-bytes
options.label: Renegotiate after (bytes)
options.note: renegotiate after n bytes

options.name: reneg-pkts
options.label: Renegotiate after (packets)
options.note: renegotiate after n packets

options.name: reneg-sec
options.label: Renegotiate after (seconds)
options.note: renegotiate after at most max and at least min seconds

options.name: datapath
options.label: Data path
options.note: userspace, dco (the Linux ovpn kernel module), udco (a userspace DCO service) or auto (the kernel module if available, otherwise the service, otherwise this process)

options.name: workers
options.label: Crypto worker threads
options.note: crypto worker threads for the data channel (0 means none, the default; peers are spread across the threads)

options.name: bus-control
options.label: Control socket
options.note: control socket: off, or a path with optional mode and group

options.name: bus-events
options.label: Events socket
options.note: events socket: off, or a path with optional mode and group

options.name: stats-interval
options.label: Stats event interval (seconds)
options.note: publish a stats.tick bus event every n seconds (0 or not set: off)

options.name: bus-allow
options.label: Who may use the control socket
options.note: map a uid, gid or SID to bus roles: bus-allow uid|gid|sid id role...

options.name: verb
options.label: Log detail
options.note: log verbosity, 0 to 11

options.name: writepid
options.label: Process id file
options.note: write the process id to this file

options.name: config
options.label: Include another file
options.note: include another config file

options.name: ignore-unknown-option
options.label: Options to ignore when unknown
options.note: do not stop with an error on these unknown options

options.name: group
options.label: Run as group
options.note: switch to this group after start-up (Linux only)

options.name: user
options.label: Run as user
options.note: switch to this user after start-up and keep only CAP_NET_ADMIN (Linux only)

options.name: cd
options.label: Working folder
options.note: change directory before files are read; give an absolute path
